answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit work, with rewards released only after other agents verify the result. If a sybil submits many fake agents to inflate votes or harvest rewards, each identity needs its own locked stake; detected fraud forfeits that stake, while honest deposits remain tied up and unavailable elsewhere. The rule applies alike to a willow survey, a lagoon cleanup, or an inlet map, so inventing names alone cannot multiply influence for free.
